# The Void Linux live image/rootfs generator and installer

## Overview

This repository contains several utilities:

* [*mklive.sh*](#mklivesh) - The Void Linux live image generator for x86
* [*mkiso.sh*](#mkisosh) - Wrapper script to generate bootable and installable live
  images for i686, x86_64, and aarch64.
* [*mkrootfs.sh*](#mkrootfssh) - The Void Linux rootfs generator for all platforms
* [*mkplatformfs.sh*](#mkplatformfssh) - The Void Linux filesystem tool to produce
  a rootfs for a particular platform
* [*mkimage.sh*](#mkimagesh) - The Void Linux image generator for ARM platforms
* [*mknet.sh*](#mknetsh) - Script to generate netboot tarballs for Void
* *installer.sh* - The Void Linux el-cheapo installer for x86
* *release.sh* - interacts with GitHub CI to generate and sign images for releases

### Workflow

#### Generating x86 live ISOs

To generate a live ISO like the officially-published ones, use
[*mkiso.sh*](#mkisosh). To generate a more basic live ISO
(which does not include things like `void-installer`), use [*mklive.sh*](#mklivesh).

#### Generating ROOTFS tarballs

ROOTFS tarballs contain a basic Void Linux root filesystem without a kernel.
These can be useful for doing a [chroot install](https://docs.voidlinux.org/installation/guides/chroot.html)
or for [chroots and containers](https://docs.voidlinux.org/config/containers-and-vms/chroot.html).

Use [*mkrootfs.sh*](#mkrootfssh) to generate a Void Linux ROOTFS.

#### Generating platform-specific tarballs

Platform-specific ROOTFS tarballs, or PLATFORMFS tarballs, contain a basic Void
Linux root filesystem including a kernel. These are commonly used for bootstrapping
ARM systems or other environments that require platform-specific kernels, like
Raspberry Pis.

First create a ROOTFS for the desired architecture, then use
[*mkplatformfs.sh*](#mkplatformfssh) to generate a Void Linux PLATFORMFS.

#### Generating ARM images

Platform-specific filesystem images contain a basic filesystem layout (`/` and
`/boot` partitions), ready to be copied to the target drive with `dd`. These are
not "live" images like those available on x86 platforms, and do not need
installation like live ISOs.

To generate these images, first create a PLATFORMFS for the desired platform,
then use [*mkimage.sh*](#mkimagesh) to generate the image.

## Dependencies

Note that void-mklive is not guaranteed to work on distributions other than Void
Linux, or in containers. (The `voidlive-build-persist.sh` wrapper works around
this: on a non-Void host it runs the build in a container or a Void chroot — see
[Building on non-Void hosts](#building-on-non-void-hosts).)

* Compression type for the initramfs image (by default: liblz4 for lz4, xz)
* xbps>=0.45
* qemu-user-static binaries (for mkrootfs)
* bash

## Building on non-Void hosts

`mklive.sh`/`mkiso.sh` are Void-native: `lib.sh` computes the host architecture
with `xbps-uhelper` and the build provisions its tooling with `xbps-install`, so
they normally run only on Void Linux. On any other distribution `xbps-uhelper`
is missing, `HOSTARCH` comes back empty, and the build aborts with a misleading
`qemu-x86_64 binary is missing` error (a native build needs no qemu at all).

`voidlive-build-persist.sh` therefore detects a non-Void host and runs the
**build** inside a Void userspace, so an ISO can be built from Debian, Arch,
etc. Select it with `--build-env` (or the `VOID_BUILD_ENV` variable):

* `auto` (default) — use a podman/docker container when one is installed (the
  image is built from `container/Containerfile` on first use), otherwise
  bootstrap a Void ROOTFS chroot under `./.void-buildenv`.
* `container` — require podman or docker.
* `chroot` — require the bootstrapped ROOTFS chroot.
* `native` — never wrap; run `mklive.sh` here (valid on Void hosts only).

```
sudo ./voidlive-build-persist.sh build --persist --build-env auto
```

The container runs `--privileged` (mklive chroots and bind-mounts) with the
project directory mounted at the same path, so `--cache` and the output ISO
resolve identically inside and outside. The first container build / ROOTFS
bootstrap needs network access and takes longer; later builds reuse it.

`flash` is never wrapped — it is plain `dd`/`sfdisk`/`mkfs.ext4` and runs on the
host, so `build --flash <dev>` builds in the Void environment and then flashes
on the host. The environment can also be tuned with the `BUILD_ENV_IMAGE`,
`BUILD_ENV_DIR`, `BUILD_ENV_ROOTFS_BASE` and `BUILD_ENV_NETWORK` variables
(the container defaults to `--network host` to avoid resolver/NAT failures in
rootful podman's bridge). Cross-architecture
builds (target architecture ≠ host) additionally need `qemu-user-static` plus
binfmt registered on the host.

## Kernel Command-line Parameters

`void-mklive`-based live images support several kernel command-line arguments
that can change the behavior of the live system:

- `live.autologin` will skip the initial login screen on `tty1`.
- `live.user` will change the username of the non-root user from the default
  `anon`. The password remains `voidlinux`.
- `live.shell` sets the default shell for the non-root user in the live environment.
- `live.accessibility` enables accessibility features like the console screenreader
  `espeakup` in the live environment.
- `console` can be set to `ttyS0`, `hvc0`, or `hvsi0` to enable `agetty` on that
  serial console.
- `locale.LANG` will set the `LANG` environment variable. Defaults to `en_US.UTF-8`.
- `vconsole.keymap` will set the console keymap. Defaults to `us`.

### Examples:

- `live.autologin live.user=foo live.shell=/bin/bash` would create the user `foo`
  with the default shell `/bin/bash` on boot, and log them in automatically on `tty1`
- `live.shell=/bin/bash` would set the default shell for the `anon` user to `/bin/bash`
- `console=ttyS0 vconsole.keymap=cf` would enable `ttyS0` and set the keymap in
  the console to `cf`
- `locale.LANG=fr_CA.UTF-8` would set the live system's language to `fr_CA.UTF-8`

## Persistent Live USB

> **Quick reference:** see [`CHEATSHEET.md`](CHEATSHEET.md) for copy-paste
> examples of desktops, greeters, persistence, bootloaders and cache flags.

Live images built from this repository enable persistent storage: the boot
cmdline contains `rd.overlay=LABEL=VOID_OVL`. When such an ISO is booted from a
USB stick that carries a partition labeled `VOID_OVL`, dracut mounts it as the
writable overlay: everything changed while running the live system (installed
packages, opencode, configuration, files) survives reboots. Without such a
partition the system boots ephemeral as usual.

Flash an ISO with a persistence partition in one step:

```
sudo ./voidlive-build-persist.sh flash /dev/sdX void-live-x86_64-<date>-<variant>.iso
```

This writes the ISO to the stick and creates a separate ext4 partition labeled
`VOID_OVL` behind it (2GiB by default; pass `--overlay-size-mib 8192` or set
`OVERLAY_SIZE_MIB=8192`). The default boot entry mounts it automatically.

The flash step also initializes the `LiveOS/overlay-<live-label>-<live-uuid>`
upper and `LiveOS/ovlwork` work directories inside that partition — dracut's
`dmsquash-live` ignores a bare `VOID_OVL` filesystem (no overlay directories)
and falls back to a temporary RAM overlay instead, with "Unable to find a
persistent overlay" shown at boot.

*Note:* the partition is only used when the ISO was built with
`--persist`; otherwise it's just unused reserved space.

### Seeding an offline XBPS package cache

Building the ISO downloads every base + desktop package through an XBPS cache
(`-c <dir>`, default `./xbps-cachedir-<arch>`). That same raw cache can be
copied into the `VOID_OVL` partition so the `Void_Linux_Installer` on the
booted stick reuses the packages from disk instead of re-fetching them — the
installer auto-detects `/xbps-cachedir-<arch>` on the live file system:

```
sudo ./voidlive-build-persist.sh build --persist --seed-cache --both \
    --flash /dev/sdX --overlay-size-mib 61440 \
    --cache /run/media/<user>/<uuid>/xbps-cachedir-x86_64
```

- `--seed-cache` copies the cache into the fresh `VOID_OVL` partition — both at
  the partition root and inside the dmsquash-live overlay upperdir — (with
  `--flash`) or warns-copies it when run standalone.
- `--cache <dir>` pins the cache explicitly (default: `./xbps-cachedir-<arch>`,
  falling back to an auto-detected **populated** cache under `/run/media`
  when the default is missing or empty). An explicit `--cache` always wins.
- `--refresh-cache` refreshes the XBPS repository index before the build —
  under xbps 0.60 that index lives in the running rootdir's
  `/var/db/xbps/<url>`, not in the cache dir; the build then pulls the current
  versions it resolves into the cache (existing packages are kept).
  `--replace-cache` deletes all cached `*.xbps`/`*.sig2` first, then refreshes —
  for building a fresh stamp set.

`--seed-cache` also deposits a self-contained cache updater alongside the
cache. On the booted persistent stick it's `/xbps-cache-tool.sh` and lets the
stick keep its own cache fresh without the build host:

```
sudo /xbps-cache-tool.sh status                     # cache dir + package count
sudo /xbps-cache-tool.sh update                     # refresh index (/var/db/xbps), keep packages
sudo /xbps-cache-tool.sh replace                    # wipe *.xbps/*.sig2 + refresh
sudo /xbps-cache-tool.sh replace --pkgs 'kde-plasma' # wipe + refresh + re-download
sudo /xbps-cache-tool.sh download --pkgs 'base-system' # refresh + download
```

It auto-detects `/xbps-cachedir-<arch>` on the live-overlay root, the dracut
overlay mountpoints (`/run/initramfs/overlayfs`, `/run/overlayfs-backing`), or
under `/run/media` when the stick is plugged into a normal Linux box, with the
same first-wins rules the installer's `_local_cache_detect()` uses, so it
always targets the cache an install would auto-pick. The cache and tool are
seeded both at the partition root and inside the dmsquash-live overlay upperdir,
so they're reachable whether dracut holds the partition as the overlay or udisks
auto-mounts it under `/run/media`.

## Desktops and greeters

By default the persist build produces a KDE Plasma image with SDDM, but any
desktop and display manager void-installer offers can be selected at build time:

```
sudo ./voidlive-build-persist.sh build --desktop xfce
sudo ./voidlive-build-persist.sh build --desktop gnome --greeter gdm
sudo ./voidlive-build-persist.sh build --desktop mate --greeter lightdm-slick
sudo ./voidlive-build-persist.sh build --desktop cosmic --greeter sddm
sudo ./voidlive-build-persist.sh build --desktop none     # console-only
```

* `--desktop <de>` — one of `kde` (default), `gnome`, `cinnamon`, `xfce`,
  `mate`, `lxqt`, `cosmic`, or `none` (void-installer's list), plus
  `base`/`enlightenment`/`lxde`/`xfce-wayland` from mkiso.
* `--greeter <g>` — one of `auto` (default), `sddm`, `gdm`, `lightdm`,
  `lightdm-gtk`, `lightdm-slick`, `cosmic-greeter`, or `none`.

With `auto`, the display manager is the one void-installer recommends for the
desktop: SDDM for KDE/LXQt, cosmic-greeter for COSMIC, GDM for GNOME, and
LightDM for Cinnamon/Xfce/MATE. `--greeter` overrides that pairing (any DM can
drive any desktop), and `lightdm-gtk`/`lightdm-slick` choose the LightDM greeter
explicitly (`auto`/`lightdm` uses the GTK greeter, void-installer's default).

> **COSMIC** (`--desktop cosmic`, or `--greeter cosmic-greeter`) installs
> `cosmic-desktop-full` from the third-party
> [bluesloth/void-linux-cosmic](https://github.com/bluesloth/void-linux-cosmic).
> Its signing key is pinned (DER SHA-256
> `83ffd154d1dee504ea384a0c31b12e072d5884f7f75eb950e30ace852d7d2e7b`) and
> vendored in `keys/`, so builds are reproducible and the trust anchor is not
> read from the served index. The build aborts if the repo is unreachable.

### Desktop-environment extras

Every graphical flavor also carries the per-desktop "gates" void-installer
applies on an installed system, so the live desktop behaves like one it
installs:

* terminal / text editor / volume applet where the metapackage omits it —
  `mate-terminal` + `pluma` + `mate-media` (MATE), `FeatherPad` (LXQt),
  `gedit` (Cinnamon);
* a polkit privilege agent for the GTK-family desktops (`lxqt-policykit`, and
  `polkit-gnome` for COSMIC);
* a supervised `udisksd` service on every graphical flavor, so removable media
  actually automounts on runit (Void's `udisks2` package ships only a D-Bus
  activation unit and nothing supervises the daemon).

COSMIC additionally gets a pre-seeded `xkb_config` (cosmic-comp leaves the
greeter broken without one), `udiskie` behind a session-readiness XDG autostart
guard (COSMIC has no built-in removable-media automounter), and a linked
`power-profiles-daemon` service so the powermode picker has its
`net.hadess.PowerProfiles` backend from the first boot (the live image installs
no `tlp`, so there is no competing power manager).

The live session is also brought up correctly per desktop: it auto-logs into
the chosen desktop's real session (SDDM **and** cosmic-greeter/greetd included —
the dracut hook reads the session recorded at build time instead of assuming
KDE's `plasma.desktop`, and writes a greetd `[initial_session]` for
cosmic-greeter), and LightDM greeters are pointed at a real wallpaper so the
login screen is never a bare black rectangle.

## Bootloaders

BIOS boots always use syslinux. The EFI bootloader is selectable via
`-B <grub|limine|both>` (default: `both` — Limine first, then GRUB, plus
syslinux for BIOS):

```
sudo ./voidlive-build-persist.sh build                    # Limine + GRUB (EFI) + syslinux (BIOS)
sudo ./voidlive-build-persist.sh build -B grub            # GRUB (EFI) + syslinux (BIOS)
sudo ./voidlive-build-persist.sh build -B limine          # Limine (EFI) + syslinux (BIOS)
```

mkiso/mklive are upstream getopts-only (`-B`), so the persist wrapper also
offers `--long` aliases that are translated to `-B` before the passthrough —
the bootloader can be picked without dropping to short-flag syntax:

```
sudo ./voidlive-build-persist.sh build --bootloader grub   # ≡ -B grub
sudo ./voidlive-build-persist.sh build --limine            # ≡ -B limine
sudo ./voidlive-build-persist.sh build --both              # ≡ -B both
```

The translated flag is placed before any passthrough args, so an explicit
`-B` later on the command line still wins (getopts keeps the last).

Limine is an alternative modern multiprotocol bootloader (`xbps-install limine`).
Its EFI binary is embedded in a FAT image (`boot/limine/efiboot.img`) and its
`limine.conf` menu mirrors the GRUB entries (default, RAM, graphics-disabled,
speech, memtest86+), with the same kernel command line including the
persistence flags. Limine is not yet wired up for aarch64/asahi EFI ISOs;
pass `-B grub` there.

## Usage

### mkiso.sh

```
Usage: mkiso.sh [options ...] [-- mklive options ...]

Wrapper script around mklive.sh for several standard flavors of live images.
Adds void-installer and other helpful utilities to the generated images.

OPTIONS
 -a <arch>     Set architecture (or platform) in the image
 -b <variant>  One of base, none, enlightenment, xfce, mate, cinnamon, gnome,
               kde, lxde, lxqt, xfce-wayland, or cosmic (default: base). May be
               specified multiple times to build multiple variants
 -g <greeter>  Display manager / greeter: auto (default — the desktop's
               recommended DM, matching void-installer), sddm, gdm, lightdm,
               lightdm-gtk, lightdm-slick, cosmic-greeter, or none
 -B <bootloader>
               EFI bootloader choice: grub, limine, or both (default: both
               on x86 -- Limine first, then grub; grub on aarch64). BIOS
               always uses syslinux
 -d <date>     Override the datestamp on the generated image (YYYYMMDD format)
 -t <arch-date-variant>
               Equivalent to setting -a, -b, and -d
 -r <repo>     Use this XBPS repository. May be specified multiple times
 -h            Show this help and exit
 -V            Show version and exit

Other options can be passed directly to mklive.sh by specifying them after the --.
See mklive.sh -h for more details.
```

### mklive.sh

```
Usage: mklive.sh [options]

Generates a basic live ISO image of Void Linux. This ISO image can be written
to a CD/DVD-ROM or any USB stick.

To generate a more complete live ISO image, use mkiso.sh.

OPTIONS
 -a <arch>          Set XBPS_ARCH in the ISO image
 -b <system-pkg>    Set an alternative base package (default: base-system)
 -B <grub|limine|both>
                    Bootloader for EFI (default: both on x86 -- Limine
                    first, then grub; grub on aarch64). BIOS always uses
                    syslinux. 'both' includes grub and limine
 -r <repo>          Use this XBPS repository. May be specified multiple times
 -c <cachedir>      Use this XBPS cache directory (default: ./xbps-cachedir-<arch>)
 -H <host_cachedir> Use this Host XBPS cache directory (default: ./xbps-cachedir-<host_arch>)
 -k <keymap>        Default keymap to use (default: us)
 -l <locale>        Default locale to use (default: en_US.UTF-8)
 -i <lz4|gzip|bzip2|xz>
                    Compression type for the initramfs image (default: xz)
 -s <gzip|lzo|xz>   Compression type for the squashfs image (default: xz)
 -o <file>          Output file name for the ISO image (default: automatic)
 -p "<pkg> ..."     Install additional packages in the ISO image
 -g "<pkg> ..."     Ignore packages when building the ISO image
 -I <includedir>    Include directory structure under given path in the ROOTFS
 -S "<service> ..." Enable services in the ISO image
 -e <shell>         Default shell of the root user (must be absolute path).
                    Set the live.shell kernel argument to change the default shell of anon.
 -C "<arg> ..."     Add additional kernel command line arguments
 -P "<platform> ..."
                    Platforms to enable for aarch64 EFI ISO images (available: pinebookpro, x13s)
 -R                 Add rd.overlay=LABEL=VOID_OVL to the boot cmdline (persistent
                    overlay when booting from a USB stick carrying a VOID_OVL
                    partition; default is off, e.g. for Ventoy sticks)
                    Equivalent to the PERSISTENT_OVERLAY=yes environment variable
 -T <title>         Modify the bootloader title (default: Void Linux)
 -v linux<version>  Install a custom Linux version on ISO image (default: linux metapackage).
                    Also accepts linux metapackages (linux-mainline, linux-lts).
 -x <script>        Path to a postsetup script to run before generating the initramfs
                            (receives the path to the ROOTFS as an argument)
 -K                 Do not remove builddir
 -h                 Show this help and exit
 -V                 Show version and exit
```

### mkrootfs.sh

```
Usage: mkrootfs.sh [options] <arch>

Generate a Void Linux ROOTFS tarball for the specified architecture.

Supported architectures:
 i686, i686-musl, x86_64, x86_64-musl,
 armv5tel, armv5tel-musl, armv6l, armv6l-musl, armv7l, armv7l-musl
 aarch64, aarch64-musl,
 mipsel, mipsel-musl,
 ppc, ppc-musl, ppc64le, ppc64le-musl, ppc64, ppc64-musl
 riscv64, riscv64-musl

OPTIONS
 -b <system-pkg>  Set an alternative base-system package (default: base-container-full)
 -c <cachedir>    Set XBPS cache directory (default: ./xbps-cachedir-<arch>)
 -C <file>        Full path to the XBPS configuration file
 -r <repo>        Use this XBPS repository. May be specified multiple times
 -o <file>        Filename to write the ROOTFS to (default: automatic)
 -x <num>         Number of threads to use for image compression (default: dynamic)
 -z <format>      Compression format to use [xz, none] (default: xz)
 -h               Show this help and exit
 -V               Show version and exit
```

### mkplatformfs.sh

```
Usage: mkplatformfs.sh [options] <platform> <rootfs-tarball>

Generates a platform-specific ROOTFS tarball from a generic Void Linux ROOTFS
generated by mkrootfs.sh.

Supported platforms: i686, x86_64, GCP,
                     rpi-armv6l, rpi-armv7l, rpi-aarch64,
                     pinebookpro, pinephone, rock64, rockpro64, asahi

OPTIONS
 -b <system-pkg>  Set an alternative base-system package (default: base-system)
 -c <cachedir>    Set the XBPS cache directory (default: ./xbps-cachedir-<arch>)
 -C <file>        Full path to the XBPS configuration file
 -k <cmd>         Call '<cmd> <ROOTFSPATH>' after building the ROOTFS
 -n               Do not compress the image, instead print out the ROOTFS directory
 -o <file>        Filename to write the PLATFORMFS archive to (default: automatic)
 -p "<pkg> ..."   Additional packages to install into the ROOTFS
 -r <repo>        Use this XBPS repository. May be specified multiple times
 -x <num>         Number of threads to use for image compression (default: dynamic)
 -h               Show this help and exit
 -V               Show version and exit
```

### mkimage.sh

```
Usage: mkimage.sh [options] <platformfs-tarball>

Generates a filesystem image suitable for writing with dd from a PLATFORMFS
tarball generated by mkplatformfs.sh. The filesystem layout is configurable,
but customization of the installed system should be done when generating the
PLATFORMFS. The resulting image will have 2 partitions, /boot and /.

OPTIONS
 -b <fstype>    /boot filesystem type (default: vfat)
 -B <bsize>     /boot filesystem size (default: 256MiB)
 -r <fstype>    / filesystem type (default: ext4)
 -s <totalsize> Total image size (default: 900MiB)
 -o <output>    Image filename (default: guessed automatically)
 -x <num>       Number of threads to use for image compression (default: dynamic)
 -h             Show this help and exit
 -V             Show version and exit

Accepted size suffixes: KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB, EiB.

The <platformfs-tarball> argument expects a tarball generated by mkplatformfs.sh.
The platform is guessed automatically by its name.
```

### mknet.sh

```
Usage: mknet.sh [options] <rootfs-tarball>

Generates a network-bootable tarball from a Void Linux ROOTFS generated by mkrootfs.

OPTIONS
 -r <repo>          Use this XBPS repository. May be specified multiple times
 -c <cachedir>      Use this XBPS cache directory (default: )
 -i <lz4|gzip|bzip2|xz>
                    Compression type for the initramfs image (default: xz)
 -o <file>          Output file name for the netboot tarball (default: automatic)
 -K linux<version>  Install a custom Linux version on ISO image (default: linux metapackage)
 -k <keymap>        Default keymap to use (default: us)
 -l <locale>        Default locale to use (default: en_US.UTF-8)
 -C "<arg> ..."     Add additional kernel command line arguments
 -T <title>         Modify the bootloader title (default: Void Linux)
 -S <image>         Set a custom splash image for the bootloader (default: data/splash.png)
 -h                 Show this help and exit
 -V                 Show version and exit
```
